title: Run a Detail Check Before You Ship
subtitle: Turn vague carefulness into a bounded verification routine.
description: Inspect a concrete artifact against a small checklist, run a second pass from a different angle, log anomalies, and improve the checklist from real misses rather than training vague hypervigilance.

lifeOsSource.hack: Improve detail work by checking a real artifact against explicit failure modes, not by trying to notice everything.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Choose an artifact or environment where errors matter, write a short checklist from known failure modes, inspect once for completeness and once from a different perspective such as data consistency or user flow, record anomalies, fix them, and update the checklist when a new recurring miss appears.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: What defect or ambiguity did the check find, which checklist item caught it, and what recurring miss should change the next review?

faq.question: Should I try to notice more details everywhere?
faq.answer: No. Use attention where the cost of an error justifies it. A bounded checklist is more actionable than staying continuously alert.
faq.answerHtml: No. Use attention where the cost of an error justifies it. A bounded checklist is more actionable than staying continuously alert.

intro.html: Attention to detail is easier to improve when the target is explicit. Instead of trying to become generally hyper-observant, define the failure modes that matter for a specific artifact and build a short verification loop around them.

sections.title: 1. Define what can go wrong
sections.html: Choose a document, dataset, screen, configuration, report, package, or other artifact. List the few mistakes that would create real rework, confusion, or risk.

sections.title: 2. Run two different passes
sections.html: First check the known failure modes systematically. Then change perspective: follow the user flow, reconcile totals, trace links, compare source and output, or inspect naming consistency.

sections.title: 3. Learn from actual misses
sections.html: Log meaningful defects and near-misses. Add a checklist item only when it catches a recurring class of error; remove checks that create noise without changing quality or decisions.

editorialCuration.reason: Replace unsupported perception statistics, fabricated improvement timelines, invented pilot outcomes, and people-observation prompts with a bounded artifact verification routine.
